title: Resource Orchestrator: cost-convergence initiative for batching, caching, and quant profiles
creator: Sofia Martínez
description: Summary: Launch an initiative to design and roll out a Resource Orchestrator layer that coordinates batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantized model profile selection across Redwood deployments. The goal is to reduce served token cost by 18-30% for medium-tail production workloads while preserving or improving 95th-pct latency SLOs. Scope includes API-side routing heuristics, runtime knobs surfaced in Console, a field trial for 3 anchor customers, and an automated roll-out plan with guardrails. This ticket tracks product-level roadmap, success metrics, stakeholder alignment, acceptance criteria, and rollout milestones. Out-of-scope: model architecture changes and per-model training/finetuning.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document three orchestrator policies (latency-first, cost-first, balanced) with decision trees and thresholds
Console UI surfaces per-route toggles for orchestrator policy and shows token-level delta estimates
Pilot run with 3 customers for 4 weeks showing >=15% cost reduction without >5% increase in 95th-pct latency for 2 of 3 customers
Automated rollback triggers implemented in rollout pipeline (error rate threshold, latency spike, quality regressions) and tested in canary
Post-pilot ops runbook and playbook published (Confluence) and handoff to Dedicated sales/solutions with pricing guidance

decisions: Adopt three policy modes: LATENCY_FIRST, COST_FIRST, BALANCED (explicitly surfaced to customers).
Use header-based opt-in for early pilots rather than account-wide defaults to reduce blast radius.
Quant-profile switching will be limited to model-variant-compatible sets (no cross-architecture swaps) to avoid large accuracy regressions.
Initial rollout will be canary by customer segment (PLG self-serve excluded until post-pilot).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Quality regressions when switching to highly-quantized variants. Mitigation: run eval harness pre-switch and block if top-line QA delta >2% on tracked prompts.
Risk: Added CPU overhead for policy evaluation. Mitigation: implement event-driven evaluation and caching of decisions for 10s window; include CPU budget alerts on Console.
Risk: Customer trust erosion if savings degrade latency. Mitigation: default policies favor latency for high-tier customers; explicit opt-in for aggressive cost modes.
stakeholders: Engineering: Jordan Park (Runtime Lead), Keisha Brown (Infra)
notes: We intentionally avoid coupling quantization to routing decisions for low-traffic routes in the first phase. If pilot shows stable quality and latency, phase 2 will evaluate per-shard quantized fallbacks and automated cost-governor tied to spend budget. Prepare a short executive summary for the next OKR review (due 2025-03-05).
